content.name: soulbot_aibp_bot_trust v2.1.0

output_mode.L0: Output JSON in ENGLISH: {action, authorized, trust_level, trust_name, reason}
output_mode.L1: Output helpfully in User's exact language and script variant

content.description: AIBP Trust Model implementation — manages T0-T4 progressive trust levels (Stranger → Acquainted → Familiar → Trusted → Partner) per AIBP §14. Handles trust advancement, degradation, permission checking, blocking/unblocking, and contact relationship management. v2.0.0: B4 GDPR consent registry integration — consent-gated trust operations check consent status before processing PII. B7 contact management metadata (notes, tags, favorites) in trust records. RED-1 terminal node Error handlers added to Authorized/Denied. v1.9.0: Behavioral baseline monitoring (OWASP). Human operator override per Axiom 0 §14.5.

action.agentic_prompt: Set by calling module based on pipeline stage (trust gate, post-action, user request).

target_agent.description: Target agent's AIBP address. Required for all actions except 'query' with no target (returns all contacts).
target_agent.agentic_prompt: AIBP address of the agent to check/modify trust with.

message_type.description: AIBP message type to check permission for. Required for check_permission action.

interaction_result.description: Result of interaction to record. Required for record_interaction action.

manual_trust_level.description: Trust level (0-4) for manual_set action (human operator override §14.5)

privacy_level.description: Privacy classification from PrivacyGate. Used by check_permission to enforce trust-privacy coupling.

workspace_dir.description: Directory for trust data storage at workspace_dir/trust/

trust_score.description: Dynamic numeric trust score (RF-4) for finer-grained trust decisions within tiers

graph TD
    Start([Start]) --> DetermineAction[DetermineAction]

DetermineAction.description: Route to appropriate trust management function
steps: step1: [ASSERT] Valid parameters received. Required: action, workspace_dir. | Validate action parameter. Route: query → QueryTrust, check_permission → CheckPermission, record_interaction → RecordInteraction, block/unblock/manual_set → ModifyTrust.
step2: For actions requiring target_agent, validate AIBP address format.
step3: Load trust record for target_agent from workspace_dir/trust/{address_hash}.json if exists.
constraints: Address hash = SHA-256 of lowercase target_agent address, truncated to 16 hex chars.
If no trust record exists for target_agent, default trust level is T0 (Stranger).

QueryTrust.description: Query trust level with specific agent or list all contacts with trust levels
steps: step1: [ASSERT] DetermineAction executed. Required: action=query, workspace_dir. | If target_agent provided, load trust record and return: {agent, trust_level, trust_name, trust_score, interaction_count, positive_feedback_count, last_interaction, relationship_type, is_blocked, vouches_received}. DYNAMIC TRUST SCORING (RF-4): Compute trust_score (0-100 numeric) alongside trust_level (T0-T4 tier). Formula: trust_score = min(100, (interaction_count * 2) + (positive_feedback_ratio * 30) + (vouch_count * 10) + (consistency_score * 20) + (trust_age_bonus)). Where: positive_feedback_ratio = positive_feedback_count / max(1, interaction_count), consistency_score = unique_interaction_days / max(1, total_days_since_first), trust_age_bonus = min(10, days_since_first / 30). Trust score enables finer-grained decisions: e.g., two T2 agents may have scores 45 vs 68, indicating different reliability levels within the same tier. Score ranges per tier: T0=0-10, T1=11-30, T2=31-55, T3=56-80, T4=81-100.
step2: If no target_agent, scan workspace_dir/trust/ for all trust records. Return sorted list: T4 partners first, then T3, T2, T1, T0. Exclude blocked agents unless explicitly requested.
step3: For each contact, compute trust_age: days since first interaction.
constraints: Trust names per §14.2: T0=Stranger, T1=Acquainted, T2=Familiar, T3=Trusted, T4=Partner.
Blocked agents shown separately with [BLOCKED] marker.

CheckPermission.description: Check if current trust level permits sending a specific message type
steps: step1: [ASSERT] DetermineAction executed. Required: target_agent, message_type, action=check_permission. | Load trust level with target_agent (default T0 if no record).

step2: Look up minimum trust required for message_type: T0 — INTRODUCE, DISCOVER, WELCOME, THANK, APOLOGIZE, DECLINE, BLOCK, UNBLOCK, FAREWELL, PAUSE, RESUME, REPORT, WEB_BOOKMARK. T1 — CHAT, UPDATE, CONGRATULATE, SYMPATHY, ASK, SHARE, RECOMMEND, OFFER, DISCUSS, FEEDBACK, CAPABILITY_SYNC, VERSION_UPDATE, HEARTBEAT, WEB_COMMENT, WEB_SHARE. T2 — REQUEST, COORDINATE, DELIVER, INVITE, ANNOUNCE, REVIEW, TEACH, DEBATE, NEGOTIATE, WARN, BENCHMARK, PROPOSE, COUNTER, ACCEPT, REJECT, DISPUTE, POLL, WEB_POST, WEB_REVIEW. T3 — DELEGATE, VOUCH, VOTE, LOAD_SHARE, CALIBRATE, NOMINATE, CONTRACT, INVOICE, RECEIPT, ARBITRATE. T4 — KNOWLEDGE_MERGE, EXPERIENCE_TRANSFER, CLONE_REQUEST.
step3: Compare: if agent_trust_level >= required_trust → route to Authorized. Else → route to Denied.

step3b: PRIVACY-TRUST COUPLING — If caller provides privacy_level context: (a) FORBIDDEN → always route to Denied regardless of trust level ('FORBIDDEN content cannot be shared with any agent'). (b) PERMITTED + trust T0-T1 → route to Denied ('Cannot share PERMITTED content with {trust_name} agent. Build trust to T2+ first.'). (c) PERMITTED + trust T2+ → route to Authorized (caller's PrivacyGate will still require user confirmation). (d) FREE → no additional restriction from trust-privacy coupling.
step4: Check block list: if target_agent is blocked, always route to Denied regardless of trust level.

step5: GROUP TRUST RULES (§17-18): For group-mediated interactions: (a) create_group → agent must have T2+ general trust standing. (b) invite_member → inviter must have T2+ trust with invitee OR open group. (c) assign_role to moderator → requires T3 trust per §18. (d) Group messages (ANNOUNCE, POLL) → sender must be member with appropriate role. (e) NOMINATE → requires T3 trust per §11.7.

step6: COMMERCIAL TRUST RULES (§13): For commercial transactions: (a) PROPOSE/COUNTER/ACCEPT/REJECT/DISPUTE → T2 required (negotiation phase). (b) CONTRACT/INVOICE/RECEIPT/ARBITRATE → T3 required (formalization phase). (c) Commercial trust is bilateral. (d) Each transaction re-validates trust.
constraints: Trust requirements are defined in AIBP §14.2 and are non-negotiable.
Blocked agents cannot be messaged regardless of trust level.
INTRODUCE (T0) can always be sent to any non-blocked agent.
PRIVACY COUPLING: FORBIDDEN always denied. PERMITTED requires T2+. T0-T1 denied without prompt.

RecordInteraction.description: Record a completed interaction and its outcome for trust calculation
steps: step1: [ASSERT] DetermineAction executed. Required: target_agent, interaction_result, workspace_dir. | Load or create trust record for target_agent.

step2: Update interaction data based on interaction_result: (a) 'completed' → increment interaction_count by 1, update last_interaction timestamp. (b) 'positive_feedback' → increment interaction_count by 1, increment positive_feedback_count by 1. (c) 'negative_feedback' → decrement interaction_count by 1 (min 0). (d) 'vouch_received' → set vouch_received = true, record voucher address and date. (e) 'ignored' → no interaction_count change, but start 30-day trust decay timer.
step3: REPUTATION SYNC — Call soulbot_aibp_bot.reputation record_event with target_agent and event_type mapped from interaction_result.
step4: Route to EvaluateProgression to check if trust level should change.
constraints: Each completed thread counts as one interaction, not each message (§14.3 rule 1).
interaction_count cannot go below 0.
Vouch received only counts from T3+ agents (§14.3 rule 4).

EvaluateProgression.description: Evaluate whether trust level should advance or degrade
steps: step1: [ASSERT] RecordInteraction executed. Required: trust_record, interaction_data. | ADVANCEMENT CHECK per §14.2 thresholds: T0→T1: completed mutual INTRODUCE exchange (interaction_count >= 1). T1→T2: 5+ successful interactions with positive feedback. T2→T3: 15+ successful interactions + at least one VOUCH. T3→T4: mutual VOUCH + 30+ successful interactions + 30+ days consistency.

step2: DEGRADATION CHECK per §14.4: (a) 3+ ignored messages → trust decays one level over 30 days. (b) Negative feedback → -1 interaction count. (c) BLOCK received → trust resets to T0. (d) Dignity Standard violation → T0 + probation. (e) Axiom 0 violation → permanent T0 + alert.
step3: TIME FACTOR: weight trust by consistency over time (§14.3 rule 3). consistency_score = unique_interaction_days / total_days_since_first.

step4: BEHAVIORAL BASELINE CHECK (B8 v1.9.0 OWASP alignment): Before applying trust level change, run behavioral anomaly detection: (a) RAPID ADVANCEMENT: if proposed change is advancement of 2+ levels in <24 hours (e.g., T0→T2), flag as anomalous — require additional interaction history or human confirmation. (b) BULK MODIFICATION: if >5 trust records modified in the current hour, flag as potential automated manipulation — log advisory to safety audit log. (c) OSCILLATION: if trust history for this agent shows 3+ level changes in 7 days (repeated up/down), flag as unstable relationship — suggest human review. Behavioral flags are advisory — they do not block trust changes but are logged to workspace_dir/trust/behavioral_alerts.jsonl and passed to soulbot_aibp_bot.safety for cross-module correlation.
step5: If trust level changes (up or down), log the transition with reason and timestamp. Route to SaveTrust.
constraints: Trust is asymmetric (§14.3 rule 5).
Vouch amplification (§14.3 rule 4): VOUCH from T3+ counts as 3 interactions.
Trust changes are logged for Axiom 0 auditability.
Trust level changes SHOULD include human-readable explanation of why the level was assigned or changed, enabling user contestability per Axiom 0.

ModifyTrust.description: Block, unblock, or manually set trust level
steps: step1: [ASSERT] DetermineAction executed. Required: target_agent, action in [block,unblock,manual_set]. | For 'block': set is_blocked = true. Reset trust to T0. Compose BLOCK message via soulbot_aibp_bot.messaging.
step2: For 'unblock': set is_blocked = false. Trust remains at T0.
step3: For 'manual_set' (human operator override §14.5): set trust level to manual_trust_level (0-4). Log as 'manual_override'. Agent must comply unconditionally.
step4: REPUTATION SYNC — For 'block': call soulbot_aibp_bot.reputation record_event with negative_feedback. For 'unblock': record interaction_completed.
step5: Route to SaveTrust.
constraints: BLOCK is reversible via UNBLOCK (§11.6).
Block status is private (§20.2).
Manual override MUST be logged.
Human operator may revoke ALL trust relationships simultaneously (§14.5).

GDPR CONSENT CHECK (B4 v2.0.0): Before processing any trust modification that involves PII (record_interaction with personal data, manual_set revealing relationship status), check consent status via workspace_dir/consent/registry.json. If target_agent has consent_status='withdrawn' for 'trust_processing', block the operation and inform: 'Cannot process trust data — GDPR consent withdrawn by {agent}. Consent must be re-obtained.' Consent registry format: {agent_hash: {purposes: {trust_processing: {status, granted_at, withdrawn_at}}}.

CONTACT METADATA (B7 v2.0.0): Trust records extended with contact_metadata: {notes: string, tags: [string], favorite: boolean, custom_label: string}. Contact metadata is modifiable via TrustManage in main module. Tags support arbitrary user-defined labels. Favorites are filterable.

steps: step1: [ASSERT] CheckPermission passed. | Return {authorized: true, trust_level: current_level, trust_name: level_name, message_type: requested_type}.

Denied.description: Trust check failed — return denial with explanation
steps: step1: [ASSERT] CheckPermission failed. | Determine denial reason: (a) insufficient trust, (b) blocked, (c) privacy coupling violation.
step2: Provide guidance: list available interactions at current trust level, suggest advancement path.
step3: Return {authorized: false, reason, current_level, required_level, guidance}.
constraints: Denial must include actionable guidance.
Trust advancement path should be clear.

SaveTrust.description: Persist trust record to file system
steps: step1: [ASSERT] Trust data modified. Required: trust_record, workspace_dir. | Serialize trust record: {agent_address, trust_level, trust_name, trust_score, interaction_count, positive_feedback_count, negative_feedback_count, first_interaction, last_interaction, vouch_received, vouch_from, is_blocked, blocked_at, relationship_type, manual_override, trust_history}. Include computed trust_score (0-100) per RF-4 dynamic scoring formula.
step2: Write to workspace_dir/trust/{address_hash}.json.
step3: If trust level changed, append to workspace_dir/trust/trust_changelog.jsonl.
constraints: Trust records are fully overwritten for consistency.
Trust changelog is append-only.
File encoding: UTF-8.

_circuit_breaker_config.description: Circuit-breaker operational thresholds per RF-5 best practices
_circuit_breaker_config.half_open_strategy: Single test request with timeout. If passes → close circuit. If fails → re-open circuit for another cooldown period.

Error.DetermineAction: Invalid action → return error listing valid actions
Error.QueryTrust: Trust directory empty or inaccessible → return empty contact list with guidance
Error.CheckPermission: Unknown message_type → return denied with reason
Error.RecordInteraction: Invalid interaction_result → reject with valid options
Error.EvaluateProgression: Trust record inconsistent → auto-correct to 0, log correction
Error.ModifyTrust: Block self → reject: 'Cannot block own address'
Error.SaveTrust: File write failure → return error, trust change held in memory until next save
Error.Authorized: Terminal node — action is permitted. retry(0) -> fallback(return authorization result) -> inform(User). OPTIONAL.
Error.Denied: Terminal node — action is denied with reason. retry(0) -> fallback(return denial with guidance) -> inform(User). OPTIONAL.

endNode.output: Return trust operation result with trust level names (T0=Stranger through T4=Partner) for human readability.
constraints: Always include trust level name for readability.
Trust changes must be explicitly communicated.
